scope: Targeted official-source and human-evidence adjudication; not exhaustive systematic review
attributionPolicy: Educational inspiration is separate from underlying efficacy evidence. No affiliation, certification or endorsement is claimed. Source linkage is independent corroboration unless explicit authorship is recorded.

decisionSemantics.supported: Retain only within stated scope and eligibility; not automatic dose authorization
decisionSemantics.revise: Replace broad educational wording with bounded runtime action
decisionSemantics.exclude: Do not use for automatic prescription; may explain why if asked

claims.educationalClaim: Nine adaptation categories help distinguish goals.
claims.population: General fitness discussion
claims.limitations: Taxonomy is not a validated screening tool or a requirement to train every quality each week.
claims.runtimeAction: Tag goal and outcome independently; retain sport/event specificity.

claims.educationalClaim: Broad-jump, grip, heart-rate recovery and field tests are suggested.
claims.population: Mixed public audience
claims.limitations: No universal pass/fail injury prediction or diagnostic thresholds established by this episode.
claims.runtimeAction: Require test protocol and provenance; no compulsory maximal test, no diagnosis or exercise clearance from generic benchmark.

claims.educationalClaim: 3–5 days/exercises/sets/reps/minutes rest is a mnemonic sample.
claims.population: Healthy adults; training experience varies
claims.limitations: No single trial validates the entire mnemonic; maximum combinations add substantial load.
claims.runtimeAction: Do not replace sport-specific supporting strength with a 3–5-day quota; separate strength load from ballistic power load.
eligibility: Verified load estimate if percentages used

claims.educationalClaim: Strength and power require different loading and movement intent.
claims.population: Healthy adults in reviewed resistance interventions
claims.limitations: Evidence for average adaptation does not establish novice entry doses or sport race transfer.
claims.runtimeAction: Allow reviewed goal-specific load range; preserve rest and stop on quality loss.

claims.educationalClaim: Hypertrophy is adaptable across loading schemes.
claims.population: Morton: 49 resistance-trained young men, 12 weeks; consensus broader healthy adults
claims.limitations: Morton compared failure-based protocols; that does not prove failure necessary. Higher weekly volume is not universal 10–20-set optimum.
claims.runtimeAction: Keep conservative individualized volume; do not force failure or bodybuilding volume for endurance support.

claims.educationalClaim: Combine aerobic and resistance work with attention to interference.
claims.population: 43 studies of healthy adults, supervised >=4 weeks
claims.limitations: Explosive strength more vulnerable than maximal strength or hypertrophy; subgroup separation does not prove a universal threshold.
claims.runtimeAction: Prioritize key quality; feasible separation is preference, not compulsory >6 h or permission for doubles.

claims.educationalClaim: Different endurance goals require different work/rest structures.
claims.population: Helgerud: 40 moderately trained healthy men; running 8 weeks
claims.limitations: VO2max result is not race-time proof; protocol cannot validate swimming, HYROX, all-out sprinting or universal frequency.
claims.runtimeAction: Use existing sport-specific trial menus and readiness gates; do not add exhaustive maximal circuits from examples.

numericParameters.testedRunningOption: 4 x 4 min at 90–95% HRmax; 3 min active recovery; 3/week in trial

claims.educationalClaim: Foundational plan is a modifiable mixed-fitness example.
claims.population: General fitness rather than event-specific athletes
claims.limitations: Fixed weekday structure and easy-volume target are not individualized workload validation.
claims.runtimeAction: Keep as attributed educational reading; no automatic replacement of current event plan or missed-session doubling.
eligibility: Explicit athlete interest in general fitness
claims.existingDossierConflict: Must not restore universal double-hard quota

claims.educationalClaim: PDF suggests 20–60 s all-out/10 s rest, 8–12 rounds and reaching HRmax.
claims.population: General fitness template
claims.limitations: Cardiac response lags short efforts; fatigue circuits are not maximal-velocity track practice.
claims.runtimeAction: Block as default sprint generator; use distance, speed quality and full recoveries for track speed.
claims.existingDossierConflict: Preserves sprint distance/open targets and full-rest rule

claims.educationalClaim: Start with goals, constraints and a structured program design process.
claims.population: General programming
claims.limitations: A process checklist does not validate an exact progression percentage.
claims.runtimeAction: Collect goal, schedule, exercise access and adherence constraints before generating; mark planner doses as JMM inference.

claims.educationalClaim: Brief deliberate breathing is proposed for post-workout downregulation.
claims.population: Remote randomized adult study; daily 5 min for one month
claims.limitations: Mood/respiratory-rate results; no significant HRV, resting-HR or sleep changes. No exercise-adaptation or race test.
claims.runtimeAction: Optional comfortable seated relaxation; no recovery-score bonus or increased training allowance. Avoid hyperventilation/retention in water, while driving or during exertion; stop if dizzy.
claims.existingDossierConflict: Reject episode inference of reliably higher HRV or faster training recovery

claims.educationalClaim: Recovery should include adequate individualized sleep.
claims.population: Mah: 11 male collegiate basketball players; 5–7-week extension after baseline
claims.limitations: 10 h in bed was study opportunity, not every athlete sleep requirement; no randomized control. Wearable stages are not diagnosis.
claims.runtimeAction: Ask about sleep need, consistency and symptoms; persistent insomnia, snoring/apnea concerns warrant clinical advice. Never replace sleep with NSDR.

claims.educationalClaim: Avoid routine immediate cold immersion when hypertrophy is priority.
claims.population: 21 active men, 12 weeks, strength twice/week; additional acute study
claims.limitations: Cold protocol attenuated adaptation; does not validate exact 6–8 h safe delay or all sport contexts.
claims.runtimeAction: Show conditional adaptation tradeoff; do not automatically prescribe extreme cold, heat/cold cycles or an exact safe window.

claims.educationalClaim: Bodyweight lb/30 fluid oz each 15–20 min is a rough mnemonic.
claims.population: Exercise fluid needs vary with athlete and environment
claims.limitations: Galpin explicitly credits other researchers; formula is not his trial. Mass alone omits sweat rate, weather, duration and overdrinking.
claims.runtimeAction: Never auto-populate hydration from this equation; use thirst fallback and measured-context plan, avoid exercise weight gain.
claims.existingDossierConflict: Retain NATA individualized hydration in nutrition-evidence.md

claims.educationalClaim: Peri-workout carbohydrate examples are rough starting heuristics.
claims.population: Athletes across sport demands
claims.limitations: Bodyweight-based peri-workout total is not g/h requirement; heat alone is not carbohydrate expenditure.
claims.runtimeAction: Use duration/intensity and practiced tolerance; preserve 30–60 g/h and up-to-90 g/h conditional branches from existing dossier.
claims.existingDossierConflict: Reject mandatory high fueling for every short/easy session

claims.educationalClaim: Food/protein adequacy matters more than a compulsory post-workout product.
claims.population: Exercising adults
claims.limitations: No universally necessary whey product, 40 g dose or narrow anabolic window.
claims.runtimeAction: Use food-first daily range; compute only from known mass; powder only as convenience.

claims.educationalClaim: Creatine is discussed for performance.
claims.population: Healthy adults; strongest use for repeated high-intensity work and resistance adaptation
claims.limitations: Not automatic endurance race or single swim-sprint benefit; weight gain and GI tolerance matter.
claims.runtimeAction: Retain optional creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day discussion, not universal 10–15 g or stack; preserve contraindication/batch-tested gates.
claims.existingDossierConflict: Keep existing direct null elite-swim evidence

claims.educationalClaim: Stimulants can support selected performance demands.
claims.population: Mostly healthy adult sport studies
claims.limitations: Sleep disruption, anxiety, GI effects and total intake can outweigh benefits; larger dose not reliably better.
claims.runtimeAction: Optional individualized lower-dose strategy per existing dossier; no default stimulant for fatigue, illness or poor sleep.

claims.educationalClaim: Educational resources discuss glutamine, alpha-GPC and tyrosine.
claims.population: Heterogeneous evidence and uses
claims.limitations: No verified basis here for universal healthy-athlete recovery stack; absence of routine recommendation is not proof every use is ineffective.
claims.runtimeAction: Do not generate these supplements or sponsor bundles; retain evidence-specific food-first AIS/IOC gate.
claims.existingDossierConflict: Preserve excluded/experimental categories rather than promoting by personality

claims.educationalClaim: Galpin coauthored a human distance-runner taper study.
claims.population: Seven collegiate distance runners, 3-week taper
claims.limitations: Small before/after study cannot prove ideal taper length or transfer across events; sex not verified in retrieved abstract.
claims.runtimeAction: Add genuine author-conducted research provenance; retain event-specific taper evidence and avoid precise performance promises.

claims.educationalClaim: Galpin coauthored randomized whole-egg versus egg-white training study.
claims.population: 30 resistance-trained young men, 12 weeks; 3 whole eggs versus 6 egg whites after training
claims.limitations: Groups differed in nutrients beyond protein; no between-group muscle-mass difference. Not proof whole foods beat all protein powders.
claims.runtimeAction: Educational food option only; no compulsory eggs, testosterone target or superiority claim.
